institutionName: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go somewhere where the culture is totally different from Denmark, and then it was a plus that Hong Kong is very international in relation to other countries in Asia.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I wish I was there for longer. It is a really good opportunity to also travel to a variety of countries outside of Hong Kong.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: They were fairly good at sending information out to us international students.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They had introduction in the beginning. The only thing that was confusing was the big campus, but they even had an app for that.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I wish they did more mingling event in the first month. You mostly had to take the initiative yourself.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: All international students get to live on campus. We live in a room with a roomie, and usually the international students are partnered up. Though some live 20 min from the school, but still in a dorm part of campus.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was a "kitchen". It had boiling water and a microwave. But I mostly just ate at the cafeterias.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It's nice that you pay for living there before you go (and its quit cheap) and then when you are living there you don't has to think about it.

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was okay for the price. It's an older building but the cleaning lady are good at their jobs!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You choose courses a bit late for my liking, but then when school start you have 2 weeks of add/drop period, so if you are unsure you can go to different courses to find out how they are like.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It's all done online and quite easy.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses that I wished for before are went there, and I didn't change them.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you are allowed to choose some "fun" courses, then do it!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was a bit worried that they would not be good at english, but most of my professors had taking education in the US or something similar, so that was not an issue. In general they were very engaging and it seemed like they actually cared about teaching us.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I only took bachelor courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I really liked their style since it mostly is a mix of midterm and final, and sometime extra assingments. Most of my exams were even multiple choise or True/false. They also say that its easy to pass courses there but difficult to get good grades. I didn't really feel that, since I got better grades there than at UCPH. Maybe the exam style was just more my liking.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
LIFS 4760 Biochemistry of diseases 
LIFS 2060 Biodiversity 
LIFS 4090 Developmental biology 
LIFS 4370 Human genetics and personalized medicine 
PPOL 2110 Science, Technology and Society in China

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Actually I liked most of them.

Biochem of diseases was interesting since we went more in depth of some specific diseases, and I really liked the exams. You just has to remember alot of drugs ect. 

I liked biodiversity since it was something totally new for me, but t was also interesting because I now know lot of fun facts abouth different species. The exams was also quit easy.

Developmental biology was propably the course i like the least. The course was a bit confusing. But the curiculum but also how the exams would be like. 

In human genetics we got to make a presentation and an assingment on SNPs which i really liked. The lectorer was also really good and engaging.

Science and technology in China was actually my "fun" course. It took out a bit more time that I thought with assingments, but looking back since I only needed to pass, I could have used less time on it. The course also focused on discussions in class which was fun and not very diffucult. The professor was my favorit one I have ever had in uni. He was very passionated about teaching.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is actually a lot of different clubs. The only thing is that the start a bit late and then with the exams weeks it was difficult to attend alot of activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did volleyball which was fun

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go hiking or go to some of the many small islands. I also went to go to Shenzhen in mainland China, Macau and Taiwan. I can recomend those places as well.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy since the university has a lot of exchange students and the city in generel is quite international.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join some of the clubs, get a buddy and attend the trips in the biginning of the semester

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The locals like to make noises (blowing their nose ect.) while the lecturer is speaking.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are very friendly and wants to talk to us. Sometimes it is just a bit difficult for them

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Remember to explore Hong Kong instead of just flying to different countries
- Bring hoodies and longer pants as well. It is not gonna be cold outside whatsoever, but sitting in the classes or the library is very cold

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not having enough time

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
